name: Cox's Bazar
summary: Home of the world's longest natural sea beach (about 120 km). A relaxed beach town with sunsets, seafood, hill and island day trips, and the best-connected beach holiday in Bangladesh.
season_note: November to March is dry and pleasant. April to May is hot. June to September is monsoon: heavy rain, rough sea and red flags on the beach.
avoid_note: Peak crowds hit on public holidays, Eid and winter weekends: book hotels early. Do not swim when the red flag is up.

reach.how: AC or sleeper coach from Dhaka (Sayedabad, Fakirapool, Kamalapur) - operators such as Hanif, S Alam, Soudia, Green Line, Saintmartin Paribahan
reach.note: Overnight coaches are the most common choice. Book ahead on weekends.

reach.how: Cox's Bazar Express via Chattogram (check Bangladesh Railway e-ticket for times and class fares)
reach.note: Fares vary by class. Seats sell out quickly.

reach.how: Dhaka (Hazrat Shahjalal) to Cox's Bazar airport - Biman, US-Bangla, Novoair
reach.note: Fastest option. Fares jump on holidays.

local.note: Agree the fare before you get in.

local.mode: Marine Drive jeep or microbus (day hire)
local.note: Good for Himchari and Inani in one day.
Short hops around the beach hotels.

attractions.name: Laboni Beach
attractions.what: The main town beach: walk the sand, paddle at the shoreline, watch the crowd and the fishing boats, and try beach snacks and horse rides.
attractions.tip: Go early morning for space and clean sand. Keep valuables at the hotel.

attractions.name: Sugandha and Kolatoli Beach
attractions.what: A quieter stretch near the hotels, good for a long walk and for taking photos with fewer people.
attractions.tip: Sunset here is excellent; plan your dinner after.

attractions.name: Himchari National Park and Waterfall
attractions.what: A hill-and-sea stop on Marine Drive with a small waterfall, a viewpoint over the water and short walks.
attractions.tip: The waterfall is weak in the dry season. Go with a jeep on a Marine Drive day.

attractions.name: Inani Beach
attractions.what: A wide, calmer beach with rock formations and coral stones, less crowded than Laboni.
attractions.tip: Tides matter: ask locals when the rocks are best seen.

attractions.name: Marine Drive (Cox's Bazar to Teknaf road)
attractions.what: Drive the road that runs between the hills and the sea, with stops for viewpoints and roadside coconut water.
attractions.tip: Start in the morning so you are not driving back in the dark.

attractions.name: Ramu Buddhist Temples
attractions.what: A group of old Buddhist monasteries and a giant Buddha statue, quiet and very different from the beach.
attractions.tip: Dress modestly and remove shoes at temples.

attractions.name: Sonadia Island
attractions.what: A boat day trip to a remote sandy island with crabs, birds and empty shores.
attractions.tip: Needs calm weather and a hired boat. Not suitable in monsoon.

attractions.name: Moheshkhali and Adinath Temple
attractions.what: Cross by boat to an island with a hilltop Hindu temple, betel-leaf farms and village roads.
attractions.tip: Combine with a trawler ride and eat at the jetty.

attractions.name: Burmese Market
attractions.what: Browse Burmese-style textiles, pearls, dried-fish and handicrafts; a lively evening market.
attractions.tip: Bargain politely. Pearls and stones: buy from reputable shops only.

attractions.name: Seafood dinner on the beach road
attractions.what: Choose fresh fish, prawn or lobster by weight and have it grilled or fried.
attractions.tip: Agree the price per kg before cooking and check the weight.

food.dish: Grilled or fried sea fish and prawn
Beef or mutton rezala with rice

budget.note: Basic rooms, AC rooms cost more on weekends.

luxury.note: Resorts with private beach and pools.

rules: Swim only in flagged safe zones and never when the red flag is flying.
Bargain for tuk-tuks and jeeps before you start.
Keep phones and wallets off the sand when you swim.
packing: Light cotton clothes and a cap
